prompts.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Original exercise-library artwork with the visual simplicity of classic black-and-white fitness instruction drawings. Crisp clean black contours, white body fill, a few light gray equipment fills, very sparse anatomical contour lines, no hatching, no gradients, no realistic rendering, no shadows. SAME faceless athletic adult male mannequin with short simple hair silhouette, bare torso, plain black shorts, simple white trainers in both panels. White background. Wide 3:2 landscape composition, two equal panels with generous gap; same camera, scale and equipment in each. No text, no labels, no arrows, no decorative borders, no muscle-color overlay. Whole person and all functional equipment visible without cropping. Exactly two arms, two legs and two hands per figure. The two panels show distinct positions of ONE repetition. Machine joints and equipment must be mechanically plausible; no body intersects objects. This is a new original illustration, not a copy of an existing illustration. Exercise: seated LOW CABLE ROW with TWO WRIST CUFF attachments, no handheld grips. Oblique side view showing both forearms and attachment details clearly. Person seated upright on a low flat bench facing right, both feet braced on foot supports, knees modestly bent, torso remains vertical. Two separate slim taut cables run diagonally slightly downward from D-rings on padded cuffs around the wrists to TWO adjacent low pulleys on a simple fixed frame at far right. Cuffs are broad black bands directly proximal to each hand; fingers stay relaxed open, the hands do NOT grip anything. Left panel: arms extended toward low pulleys with elbows slightly unlocked; shoulders remain relaxed. Right panel: elbows pulled close along sides, bent near 90 degrees with cuffs next to lower ribs, arms not behind torso, chest unchanged, no backward lean. Cables remain attached to cuff D-rings in both panels. Keep the distance between bench and low pulleys the same. Minimum equipment detail necessary to understand the cuff connection.
